_what: Curated timeline of the Planet Nine literature, for the 'who supports it' and 'what is the consensus' views.
_caution: 'stance' is our editorial reading of each abstract, not a label the authors chose. Say so on the site.
Crossref citation counts undercount astronomy, which cites heavily through arXiv and NASA ADS. Use them as relative weight, not absolute impact.
Every summary below was checked against the paper's own abstract (or full text) in October 2026, except where summary_checked_against_abstract is false.
This is a deliberately chosen ~32-paper sample of a literature with hundreds of entries. It is not a census, and counting stances here does not measure community opinion.

_stance_values.supports: argues the clustering is real and a planet is the best explanation
_stance_values.against: argues the clustering is an artefact of how we searched, or rules out parameter space
_stance_values.alternative: accepts the signal but proposes something other than a planet
_stance_values.neutral: characterises, constrains or supplies data without taking a side

papers.label: Morbidelli & Levison 2004
papers.title: Scenarios for the Origin of the Orbits of the Trans-Neptunian Objects 2000 CR<sub>105</sub>and 2003 VB<sub>12</sub>(Sedna)
papers.summary: Before the Planet Nine hypothesis: of four ways to lift 2000 CR105's closest point out of Neptune's reach, only a passing star works. A solar-mass star passing about 800 AU away moves only objects beyond about 200 AU, matching CR105 and the newly found Sedna (2003 VB12).

papers.label: Luhman 2014 (WISE)
papers.title: A SEARCH FOR A DISTANT COMPANION TO THE SUN WITH THEWIDE-FIELD INFRARED SURVEY EXPLORER
papers.summary: An all-sky infrared search for a distant companion to the Sun by its parallactic motion finds nothing to W2 = 14.5: no Saturn analog within 28,000 AU and no Jupiter analog within 82,000 AU (26,000 AU for a Jupiter-mass brown dwarf on fainter models). A planet of a few Earth masses is far below this reach.

papers.label: Trujillo & Sheppard 2014
papers.title: A Sedna-like body with a perihelion of 80 astronomical units
papers.summary: Discovery of 2012 VP113. First to point out that the distant objects share an argument of perihelion, and to suggest a super-Earth as the cause.

papers.label: Batygin & Brown 2016
papers.title: EVIDENCE FOR A DISTANT GIANT PLANET IN THE SOLAR SYSTEM
papers.summary: The founding paper. Six distant objects share an orbital orientation, and a ~10 Earth-mass planet on an anti-aligned orbit reproduces it.

papers.label: Fienga et al. 2016 (Cassini)
papers.title: Constraints on the location of a possible 9th planet derived from theCassinidata
papers.summary: Cassini ranging to Saturn narrows where a massive planet could sit without visibly perturbing the giant planets.

papers.label: Cowan et al. 2016 (CMB)
papers.title: COSMOLOGISTS IN SEARCH OF PLANET NINE: THE CASE FOR CMB EXPERIMENTS
papers.summary: Proposes millimetre-wave cosmology surveys as an independent search channel.

papers.label: Linder & Mordasini 2016
papers.title: Evolution and magnitudes of candidate Planet Nine
papers.summary: Thermal-evolution models predicting the planet's radius, temperature and brightness. The source of most 'what would it look like' numbers.

papers.label: Malhotra et al. 2016
papers.title: CORRALLING A DISTANT PLANET WITH EXTREME RESONANT KUIPER BELT OBJECTS
papers.summary: Period ratios among the extreme objects look like resonances with an unseen planet near 665 AU.

papers.label: Brown & Batygin 2016
papers.title: OBSERVATIONAL CONSTRAINTS ON THE ORBIT AND LOCATION OF PLANET NINE IN THE OUTER SOLAR SYSTEM
papers.summary: Maps which parts of the predicted orbit existing surveys have already searched and excluded.

papers.label: Fortney et al. 2016
papers.title: THE HUNT FOR PLANET NINE: ATMOSPHERE, SPECTRA, EVOLUTION, AND DETECTABILITY
papers.summary: Predicts the planet's atmosphere and spectrum, and which wavelengths would detect it.

papers.label: Millholland & Laughlin 2017
papers.title: Constraints on Planet Nine’s Orbit and Sky Position within a Framework of Mean-motion Resonances
papers.summary: Fits the planet's orbit by requiring mean-motion resonances with the known extreme objects.

papers.label: Shankman et al. 2017 (OSSOS VI)
papers.title: OSSOS. VI. Striking Biases in the Detection of Large Semimajor Axis Trans-Neptunian Objects
papers.summary: The clustering may be a selection effect. Surveys point where it is convenient to point, and that alone can shape the sample.

papers.label: Becker et al. 2018 (2015 BP519)
papers.title: Discovery and Dynamical Analysis of an Extreme Trans-Neptunian Object with a High Orbital Inclination
authors: Hsing Wen 省文 Lin 林
papers.summary: 2015 BP519's 54-degree inclination is difficult to produce without a massive distant perturber.

papers.label: Madigan et al. 2018
papers.title: On the Dynamics of the Inclination Instability
papers.summary: A self-gravitating population of distant bodies can tilt and align itself with no planet involved.

papers.label: Sefilian & Touma 2019
papers.title: Shepherding in a Self-gravitating Disk of Trans-Neptunian Objects
papers.summary: A massive self-gravitating disk of small bodies can produce the same clustering with no planet.

papers.label: Brown & Batygin 2019
papers.title: Orbital Clustering in the Distant Solar System
papers.summary: Quantifies the significance of the clustering after modelling known survey biases: about 1 in 500 by chance.

papers.label: Batygin et al. 2019 (review)
papers.title: The planet nine hypothesis
papers.summary: The definitive review. Revises the planet to 5-10 Earth masses, a = 400-800 AU, e = 0.2-0.5, i = 15-25 degrees, explaining clustering beyond a ~ 250 AU.

papers.label: Zderic et al. 2020
papers.title: Apsidal Clustering following the Inclination Instability
papers.summary: Shows the inclination instability also produces clustering of the longitude of perihelion, for a while, in idealised simulations; not of the orbital poles.

papers.label: Fienga et al. 2020 (INPOP19a)
papers.title: New constraints on the location of P9 obtained with the INPOP19a planetary ephemeris
papers.summary: Updated planetary ephemerides further restrict where a massive perturber can hide.

papers.label: Scholtz & Unwin 2020
papers.title: What if Planet 9 is a Primordial Black Hole?
papers.summary: Same mass, same orbit, but a grapefruit-sized primordial black hole instead of a planet.

papers.label: Napier et al. 2021
papers.title: No Evidence for Orbital Clustering in the Extreme Trans-Neptunian Objects
authors: Hsing Wen 省文 Lin 林
papers.summary: Pooling three surveys with characterised detection efficiency, the clustering is not statistically significant.

papers.label: Brown & Batygin 2021
papers.title: The Orbit of Planet Nine
papers.summary: Bias-corrected orbit fit; clustering significant at 99.6% confidence. Headline values are 6.2 Earth masses, a = 380 AU, i = 16 degrees, q = 300 AU. The site's default planet uses this paper's full marginalized posterior instead (Figure 8), because it is the only published set that includes both angles needed to place it on the sky.

papers.label: Naess et al. 2021 (ACT)
papers.title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: A Search for Planet 9
papers.summary: A blind millimetre-wave search over 18,000 square degrees finds no significant detection, rules out roughly 17% (5 Earth masses) or 9% (10 Earth masses) of the parameter space, and lists ten weak candidates for follow-up.

papers.label: Brown et al. 2022 (ZTF search)
papers.title: A Search for Planet Nine using the Zwicky Transient Facility Public Archive
papers.summary: A direct search of the ZTF archive finds no candidate to V = 20.5, ruling out 56% of the predicted Planet Nine parameter space.

papers.label: Bernardinelli et al. 2022 (DES)
papers.title: A Search of the Full Six Years of the Dark Energy Survey for Outer Solar System Objects
papers.summary: 815 TNOs from six years of DES with a published bias model. Primarily a catalogue paper, but it reports that its 16 extreme objects (a > 150 AU, q > 30 AU) are consistent with azimuthal isotropy.

papers.label: Brown & Mathur 2023
papers.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics as an Alternative to the Planet Nine Hypothesis
papers.summary: Modified gravity (MOND), proposed to explain galaxy rotation without dark matter, would line up the long axes of the distant orbits with the direction of the galactic centre and cluster them, an alternative explanation for the anomalies with no ninth planet.

papers.label: Brown & Batygin 2024 (Pan-STARRS1 search)
papers.title: A Pan-STARRS1 Search for Planet Nine
papers.summary: Rules out the Brown & Batygin (2021) Planet Nine to a 50% completion depth of V = 21.5. With ZTF and DES, 78% of the predicted parameter space is now excluded; what remains is faint and near where the northern galactic plane crosses the ecliptic.

papers.label: Vokrouhlický et al. 2024
papers.title: Testing MOND on Small Bodies in the Remote Solar System
papers.summary: The first solar-system test of MOND at the weak accelerations where it departs from Newton. Simulating bodies scattered outward over the Sun's lifetime, the popular AQUAL form fails to reproduce the long-period and Oort-cloud comets seen from Earth, and the orbits of the detached disk (perihelion > 38 AU). Screened versions of MOND are not ruled out.

papers.label: Pfalzner et al. 2024
papers.title: Trajectory of the stellar flyby that shaped the outer Solar System
papers.summary: Thousands of flyby simulations find that a star of about 0.8 solar masses passing 110 AU from the Sun at an inclination of about 70 degrees reproduces the trans-Neptunian populations, including the distant detached objects and the retrograde ones. Predicts Rubin will find distant and retrograde objects relatively common.

papers.label: Phan et al. 2025 (IRAS/AKARI)
papers.title: A search for Planet Nine with IRAS and AKARI data
papers.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia
papers.summary: One far-infrared candidate from two all-sky surveys 23 years apart, implying 500-700 AU and 7-17 Earth masses. Two detections cannot fix an orbit, so this stays a candidate until followed up.

papers.label: Chen et al. 2025 (Ammonite)
papers.title: Discovery and dynamics of a Sedna-like object with a perihelion of 66 au
papers.summary: Discovery of 2023 KQ14, a Sedna-like object with q = 66 AU and a = 252 AU. Its orbit does not align with the other Sedna-like objects, and its long-term stability favours a hypothetical planet on a larger orbit (about 500 AU) rather than a closer one.

papers.label: Cheng, Li & Yang 2026 (2017 OF201)
papers.title: Discovery of a Dwarf Planet Candidate in an Extremely Wide Orbit: 2017 OF201
papers.summary: A roughly 700 km dwarf-planet candidate on an 830 AU orbit with perihelion at 45 AU (posted May 2025). Its longitude of perihelion lies outside the observed clustering, which the authors call a challenge to the dynamical evidence for Planet Nine.
